name: Salt (table, sea, Himalayan)
native_basis_label: food-grade salt as placed on the market (dry)
scope_note: Covers table salt, sea salt, and Himalayan/rock salt. Lead is a form_split refined (1000) vs unrefined (2000) per EU 2023/915; certification applies the form matching the product. Salt is an independent mineral row (not plant-uptake); cadmium/arsenic/mercury bind the Codex-aligned food-grade-salt limits. Aluminium is additive-permitted anti-caking, managed by additive law and TWI.

Pb.basis: food-grade salt as placed on the market (dry)
Pb.instrument: EU Reg. 2023/915 — lead in salt, split refined (general food-grade) vs unrefined (fleur de sel, grey salt, manually harvested). The strictest sovereign salt-lead limit; Codex STAN 193 sets 2 mg/kg, so the EU refined value governs.

forms.form: unrefined salt (fleur de sel, grey salt, manually harvested sea salt)

stricter_unselected.basis: food as listed in Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule; source unit mg/kg
stricter_unselected.scope: Salt, food grade, other than salt from marshes, food grade

Cd.basis: food-grade salt (dry); Codex-aligned 0.5 mg/kg, concurred by many jurisdictions

tAs.basis: food-grade salt (dry); total arsenic, EU Reg. 2025/1891 with FSANZ concurrence at 500

iAs.basis: food-grade salt (dry); inorganic arsenic. Israel FCS 2016 sets an explicit inorganic-arsenic salt limit (500 ug/kg), coincident with the total-As ceiling (iAs <= tAs).

tHg.basis: food-grade salt (dry); total mercury, EU Reg. 2022/617 with FSANZ concurrence at 100

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is the organomercury speciation of mercury and is arithmetically bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg); a mineral salt carries no mercury source and no methylmercury formation pathway, and salt mercury is regulated as total mercury, which the tHg standard caps, bounding any organomercury fraction.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-Hg salt standard (EU 2022/617, 100 ug/kg); no methylmercury salt ML anywhere

Ni.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a nickel maximum level for salt. Unrefined rock and sea salts can carry trace geologic nickel; it is screened rather than assigned an invented number.
Ni.reference_method: Total-nickel screen (ICP-MS); no sovereign salt nickel ML.
Ni.trigger: periodic nickel screen; flag on anomalous elevation

Sn.rationale: No tin source in a boxed/bagged mineral salt; tin is a tinplate-can migration pathway only.
Sn.reference_method: Packaging control (non-tinplate); periodic ICP-MS tin verification.
Sn.regulatory_basis: No salt tin ML; canned-food 250 mg/kg limit is can-only

Al.rationale: Aluminium in salt derives from permitted anti-caking additives (e.g. sodium aluminosilicate, GRAS in US table salt per 21 CFR 182.2727), not contamination, and is managed by additive law plus intake against the EFSA/JECFA TWI, not by a per-food contaminant maximum level. Matches the existing salt/Al determination in standards-not-material.csv.
Al.reference_method: Managed by additive law + TWI; periodic screen.
Al.regulatory_basis: Al managed by additive law (US 21 CFR 182.2727; EU 1333/2008) + TWI; no salt contaminant ML
Al.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (lists no Al); US 21 CFR 182.2727; Codex; JECFA/EFSA TWI

Cr.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a total-chromium food maximum level (chromium(III) is an essential nutrient). Trace chromium in salt is geologic. Screened as the substrate for reflex Cr-VI speciation.
Cr.reference_method: Total-chromium screen; substrate for reflex Cr-VI speciation.
Cr.trigger: reflex Cr-VI speciation only if total chromium is anomalously elevated

Cr-VI.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is the Cr(VI) speciation of chromium and is bounded by the total-chromium control (Cr-VI <= total Cr), which is screened for salt; no jurisdiction sets a Cr-VI food maximum level. There is no chromium adulteration pathway in a mineral salt (unlike turmeric/chili, salt is not colour-adulterated with lead chromate), so any trace chromium is geologic chromium(III). Rebuttable if a routed source reports hexavalent chromium in salt.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Bounded by the total-chromium screen; no routine Cr-VI speciation, reflex only on anomalously elevated total chromium.
Cr-VI.regulatory_basis: No Cr-VI food ML anywhere; bounded by total chromium (Cr-VI <= total Cr); no chromate-adulteration pathway in salt

method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; explicit-id lookup; legislated product-form splits preserved; dried-spice basis discipline)
